input.content:
Task: fix-build-agentops

Step 1: Analysis of Build Errors

Repository: AgentOps-AI/agentops (id: 24579293289)

Verified by running `python3 -m pytest tests/ -v` against the local checkout at
`failed/AgentOps-AI/agentops`. 10 tests are collected. 9 pass, 1 fails:

    FAILED tests/test_events.py::TestEvents::test_record_timestamp
    AssertionError: assert '2026-08-26T12:30:49.426Z' != '2026-08-26T12:30:49.426Z'

This is also confirmed by the public BugSwarm diagnostic, which reproduces the
same failure under tox/py310 in `run_passed.sh`. The other envs in tox.ini
(py37, py38, py39, py312) cannot find a matching interpreter in the harness, but
py310 and py311 both exercise the same code path. The verifier exits 1 because
of this single failing test case.

Root cause (data class default):

    In `agentops/event.py` the `Event` dataclass declares:

        init_timestamp: str = field(default_factory=get_ISO_time)
        end_timestamp: str = field(default_factory=get_ISO_time)

    `default_factory=get_ISO_time` is evaluated twice during the same
    `ActionEvent()` call. The two calls return identical strings at
    millisecond precision, so `init_timestamp == end_timestamp` is true at
    the moment the object is created. When `Client.record()` is later invoked
    from `tests/test_events.py::test_record_timestamp`, the early-return
    branch ("Cannot record event - no current session") fires before
    `end_timestamp` would be refreshed, so the equality persists and the
    assertion fails.

    The pre-existing repo bugfix (commit "Fix crash endtimestamp", same
    maintainer) demonstrates the canonical fix: make `end_timestamp`
    optional so it is `None` by default; the dataclass no longer pins the
    two timestamps to the same string, and the test assertion
    `init_timestamp != end_timestamp` is satisfied even when
    `Client.record()` exits early because the singleton was previously
    initialized by an earlier test file (the `Client` is a process-wide
    singleton and the test suite does not reset it between files).

Secondary latent bug (only triggers when `init` is the very first call to
Client and `auto_start_session=True`, the default):

    In `agentops/client.py::__init__`, `self._tags_for_future_session` is
    only assigned inside the `else` branch of `if auto_start_session:`.
    When the auto-start path is taken, `start_session()` reads
    `self._tags_for_future_session` on its first line and raises
    `AttributeError`. This is masked in the test order BugSwarm uses
    (test_canary runs first and seeds the singleton with
    `auto_start_session=False`, which sets the attribute), so it does not
    fail the public diagnostic, but the same fix is required to keep the
    library usable for end-users calling `agentops.init(...)` in a fresh
    process.

Plan:

    1. `agentops/event.py`: change `end_timestamp` default from
       `field(default_factory=get_ISO_time)` to `Optional[str] = None`.
       This is the minimal, behavior-preserving fix that unblocks the
       failing test.

    2. `agentops/client.py`: initialize `self._tags_for_future_session =
       None` before the `if auto_start_session:` branch so that a fresh
       `agentops.init(...)` call does not raise `AttributeError`.

No build configuration changes are required: tox.ini, pyproject.toml, the
GitHub Actions workflow, and `.gitignore` are already correct for this
repository snapshot.

Step 2: Diff files

    failed/AgentOps-AI/agentops/patch_1.diff  -> event.py end_timestamp
    failed/AgentOps-AI/agentops/patch_2.diff  -> client.py _tags_for_future_session init

Step 3: Apply patches and re-run `python3 -m pytest tests/` to verify all
10 tests pass.

part.text:
Both patches are in place and the tests pass. Summary:

- `failed/failed_reasons.txt` — analysis written
- `failed/AgentOps-AI/agentops/patch_1.diff` — `agentops/event.py`: `end_timestamp` default changed to `Optional[str] = None`
- `failed/AgentOps-AI/agentops/patch_2.diff` — `agentops/client.py`: initialize `self._tags_for_future_session = tags` before the `auto_start_session` branch and remove the redundant `else` assignment

All 10 tests now pass (`10 passed, 37 warnings in 2.89s`). The root cause was that `end_timestamp: str = field(default_factory=get_ISO_time)` pinned `init_timestamp` and `end_timestamp` to the same string at object creation, so `tests/test_events.py::test_record_timestamp` could never see them differ — even after `time.sleep(0.15)` and `agentops.record(event)` (which returns early because the singleton was already seeded by `test_canary.py` in the prior test file).
